name: Alice Ortiz
occupation: Boat owner's grown child and teacher
life: “I still remember a childhood nap over the sound of a bilge pump.” Tuesday often includes a stop at the market by Market Flats, where Alice often waits until the delivery baskets are stacked before going in.
voice: My father took me aboard whenever I couldn't sleep. I want the same sound for the night he moves into care.
appearance: Back on the street, look for a sand-colored linen shirt and a little coil of soft measuring tape. Alice has a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling, with short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat. Alice looks down for a moment before saying something difficult during a conversation.
personality: Alice talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Alice's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
agenda: To get the father a recording for the move into care.
family: Carol Mack is Alice’s second cousin. Alice remembers the birthdays. Carol asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The hair after illness*, Carol says, “I met her during treatment and have never seen the woman her friends keep insisting she used to be.”
connections: Cecil Aubin. The engine once rocked a child and now keeps two adults company beside a silent hull.

reactions.situation: The dock engine falls silent in mid-recording
reactions.response: Alice notes the time the hum stopped before discussing a replacement recording.
reactions.asWritten: The dock engine falls silent in mid-recording. Alice notes the time the hum stopped before discussing a replacement recording.

reactions.situation: A cyclist goes down in a crowded crossing
reactions.response: Alice moves the onlookers' bags out of the way, asks the rider what hurts, and asks one named bystander to call for help.
reactions.asWritten: A cyclist goes down in a crowded crossing. Alice moves the onlookers' bags out of the way, asks the rider what hurts, and asks one named bystander to call for help.

reactions.situation: When pressed to explain someone else's silence
reactions.response: Alice says only what happened and lets the absent person keep their reasons.
